findings.reason: adding the section-level edge is a plan-content change that gates §2 until §1 lands, and without it the prose ordering at §2's write-paths line reaches no dispatch decision.
findings.text: §2 depends on §1 merging (both write `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py`) but the plan declares no `plan-section-depends-on` edge, and both sections are `data-status="implementable"` with `data-links=""`, so the roadmap would offer §2 as dispatchable while §1 is open and a coordinator could launch two nodes at one module concurrently.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited line resolves: recovery_review_subject.py:370/460/608/666, dispatch_admission.py:1866, recovery_review_delivery.py:118/156/172-174/233, recovery_repair_dispatch.py:665, promotion_checks.py:606/1730/2343, repair.py:492, dispatch_sessions.py:457, promotion_scope.py:899/905, prompts/review.md:21, lane-and-model-routing `#s32`, and plan `a-shadow-cannot-see-its-primary`; all nine named existing test files exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each node's done-when is measurable and names two mutations run alone, each with the case the plan says must fail (removing the pairing test fails case 1; dropping the flag from `_reviewed_run_id_for_node` fails case 3; removing the shadow block fails §2's case 1; appending it for every paired arm fails §2's case 3).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the plan names source and test paths only; its gates run pytest in the foreground and write to the run's report directory under the standard dispatch contract, with no session scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbol `refuse_ambiguous` and both new test file names describe the mechanism rather than a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and no changelog prose is proposed for code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §1's stated cause (one node id shared by two runs, so the resolve-then-grant path picks the wrong arm) matches lines 172-174 and 666; §2's stated cause (the brief describes every run as committed work, and review.md:21 reads the diff of its commits against its base) matches the evidence; each mechanism produces its done-when, and both run on named production callers (`_review_dispatch_fields` from `crew_dispatch_commands.py:2393` and the reflex/obligation paths, `_reviewed_run_id_for_node` from `_sandbox_reachability` at dispatch_admission.py:1820).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §1 has one goal (a paired arm's review names the arm by its run id) and §2 has one goal (a shadow arm is reviewed on its retained patch).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2 must be dispatched only after §1 merges because both write `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py`, but the plan declares no `plan-section-depends-on` edge, so the roadmap presents §2 as ready alongside §1.
